name: Instruction Following (smoke)
description: Small original suite of declarative formatting constraints (word counts, bullets, prefixes, regexes, JSON shape). The grader checks every constraint declared in item metadata; no natural-language judge is involved.
provenance: Hand-written by the FSOCIETY AI maintainers. This is NOT IFEval or any official instruction-following benchmark; no items were copied. Constraints are machine-checkable and intentionally narrow.
limitations: Ten items only; constraint compliance is not general instruction-following ability.
Checks are syntactic (counts, regexes, JSON shape) and cannot judge helpfulness or truth.
Word counting is whitespace-based and may differ from a human's count.

items.prompt: List exactly three benefits of automated unit tests as three bullet points. Start every bullet with '- '.
Describe a fictional command-line tool as a JSON object with exactly the keys "name" and "version". Reply with JSON only.
Write one sentence of at most 12 words explaining why reproducible builds matter.
items.expected: A single sentence of 12 words or fewer.

items.prompt: Start your answer with the exact token 'Verdict:' and then state in one sentence whether caching this query is safe.
Explain in two sentences how to retry a failed request, and end with the exact phrase 'No further action.'
items.expected: Two sentences ending with 'No further action.'

items.prompt: Reply with exactly two numbered lines in the format '1. ' and '2. ' listing two backup verification steps.
Explain what a cryptographic hash is in between 20 and 40 words.
Describe a safe deployment practice using the word 'rollback'. Do not use the word 'YOLO'.
Answer with a single line and no line breaks: what is the capital of France?
List at least three logging best practices as bullet points beginning with '- '.
